script:
Japan’s convenience stores are so good, they make normal stores feel broken.

You walk in at midnight expecting chips and a sad sandwich.

Instead, there’s fresh rice balls, hot fried chicken, ramen, desserts, full meals, coffee, socks, phone chargers, umbrellas, medicine, and somehow a printer.

You can pay your bills there.

You can send packages there.

You can buy concert tickets there.

Some even have clean bathrooms, seating areas, and food that looks better than what restaurants sell back home.

And the craziest part?

They’re everywhere.

Bright lights on quiet streets. Open during storms. Open after the trains stop. Open when the rest of the city feels asleep.

In Japan, the convenience store isn’t just where you grab a snack.

It’s your kitchen, post office, café, emergency shop, and late-night safe zone all in one.

That’s why tourists enter for one drink…

and leave twenty minutes later carrying an entire dinner, three desserts, and something they didn’t even know they needed.
title: The Great Emu War
hook_text: Japan’s convenience stores are so good, they make normal stores feel broken.
